title: Fist of the North Star: Lost Paradise
subtitle: Kenshiro enters a city built for more than fighting

body: Fist of the North Star: Lost Paradise is Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio's PlayStation 4 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 8 March 2018. Kenshiro explores the city of Eden in a story based on Buronson and Tetsuo Hara's manga. The studio brings systems familiar from Yakuza into the wasteland, combining violent martial-arts encounters with side activities and local personalities. The contrast is deliberate. A world associated with devastating punches also contains people asking for smaller favours, giving the player reasons to return to the city between journeys through the surrounding ruins.

Combat centres on Hokuto Shinken and its hidden channeling points, with attacks leading into spectacular finishing sequences. Experience and abilities develop Kenshiro's options as enemies and situations become more demanding. Outside those fights, Eden offers activities such as bartending and baseball, allowing the character's strength to take on deliberately comic uses. The player moves between the serious struggle of the main story and smaller encounters that change its tone. That alternation gives the adaptation a particular identity, expressing the manga's excess through both brutal action and the unexpected business of everyday life.

Jun Orihara and Nobuhiro Suzuki directed, with Masayoshi Yokoyama contributing to production and writing. The soundtrack includes work by Hidenori Shoji and other Ryu Ga Gotoku composers. Salvaged arcade machines allow older Sega games to be played, including Space Harrier and Out Run, linking the wasteland to another part of the publisher's history. International release followed in October 2018. Lost Paradise works as a meeting of two recognisable identities: the powers and imagery of Fist of the North Star are organised through the city, diversions and character encounters associated with the studio's games.
